summary.text: Caylin Young is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 45 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He is on the November ballot with fellow incumbent Jackie Addison, Democrat Chanel Branch and Green Party candidate Renaud Brown for the district's three seats.
He is an attorney who has worked for the ACLU of Maryland and the City of Baltimore, and he serves on the Ways and Means Committee.

paragraphs.text: Caylin Young was born in Baltimore and graduated from Baltimore City College in 2005.
He earned a B.S. in mathematics from Hampton University in 2010 and a J.D. from the University of Baltimore School of Law in 2016.

Young taught mathematics in Baltimore City Public Schools, worked as a legislative assistant in the Maryland House of Delegates, and served as a community outreach coordinator for Senate President Pro Tem Nathaniel McFadden, according to his legislative biography.

He was a legal fellow for U.S. Senator Cory Booker and later worked for the ACLU of Maryland, first as public policy counsel and then as director of public policy, and as director of legislative affairs for the City of Baltimore.
Young is deputy director of the City of Baltimore's Office of Equity and Civil Rights, a position the legislative biography dates from 2021.
Young assumed office on January 11, 2023, according to Ballotpedia.
The General Assembly website lists him as a member of the Ways and Means Committee.
